ruleset.name: KernDXFrameworkPackageSide
ruleset.description: Framework-internal rules. Universal hygiene that applies to both framework and subscriber code. Excludes the "use the framework API instead of the platform primitive" rules that the framework itself necessarily violates to implement those APIs.

rule.name: KernTriggerMustDelegate
rule.message: Trigger must delegate to new TRG_Dispatcher().run(). No other logic allowed in trigger body.
rule.description: Trigger files must contain only `new TRG_Dispatcher().run()` (or `new kern.TRG_Dispatcher().run()`); the rule accepts any `run()` call as that delegation. Any additional logic — SOQL, DML, method calls, variable declarations — violates the framework's trigger delegation pattern. Every statement at the top level of the trigger body other than that call is reported, including a loop or branch that wraps it; PMD places a trigger's statements directly under its synthetic invoke method, so the rule matches there. A trigger whose body never calls `run()` at all (empty, comment-only, or logic with no dispatcher call) is also reported once, at the trigger itself: it runs none of its configured trigger actions.

rule.name: KernRestResourceNaming
rule.message: @RestResource classes must follow the REST_* naming convention and delegate to API_Dispatcher.
rule.description: Classes annotated with @RestResource must follow the REST_* naming convention. REST_* classes serve as thin routing layers that delegate to API_Dispatcher.processInboundService(), with business logic in API_* classes extending API_Inbound.

rule.name: KernInvocableClassNeedsNoArgConstructor
rule.message: Class declares @InvocableVariable fields but no visible no-arg constructor. Flow/Process instantiation fails at run time; declare an explicit public no-arg constructor alongside the other constructors.
rule.description: Apex classes that expose @InvocableVariable properties (Flow / Process inputs or outputs) are instantiated through their no-arg constructor at run time. Declaring only argument-bearing constructors removes the implicit no-arg constructor, and a private no-arg constructor is not visible to Flow — either way invocation throws at run time. Declare an explicit public no-arg constructor alongside any other constructor. A class that declares no constructor at all keeps the implicit no-arg constructor and is compliant.

rule.name: KernNoLegacyAssert
rule.message: Legacy System.assert*() methods are not allowed. Use Assert.isTrue(), Assert.areEqual(), Assert.areNotEqual(), etc.
rule.description: The legacy System.assert(), System.assertEquals(), and System.assertNotEquals() methods should be replaced with the modern Assert class methods (Assert.isTrue, Assert.areEqual, etc.) which provide clearer method names and better failure messages.

rule.name: KernNoCoverageTheatre
rule.message: Test method exhibits a coverage-theatre pattern (no assertions, empty catch, Boolean exceptionThrown flag, or Assert.isNotNull after TST_Builder.build()).

property.name: xpath

rule.name: KernNoBooleanExceptionThrown
rule.message: A test must not rely on a variable set inside catch to detect that an exception was thrown (Boolean flag, captured Exception, Assert.isNull/isNotNull on it). Put Assert.fail(''Should throw ...'') inside the try after the call and assert the type inside the catch with Assert.isInstanceOfType(error, ExceptionClass.class, ...).

rule.name: KernCoverageExemptRequiresReason
rule.message: @SuppressWarnings(''PMD.KernNoCoverageTheatre'') blocks a priority-1 quality rule. Add a comment above the annotation explaining why the exemption is legitimate, and narrow the suppression to the specific method.
